note: Both sets capture the controller goals, operating ranges, filter type and variable definitions accurately, but Set A additionally includes the important fact that generator speed measurement is the sole feedback input for both controllers and that nacelle-yaw regulation was not developed. Set B omits both of these and instead adds a near-trivial claim that the baseline control system uses a conventional design approach. Set A's weakness is redundancy: the feedback-input fact is stated four times (per controller, with two different condition fields) and the filter-type fact twice. Set B repeats the nonpower-production claim under two entity names while missing the feedback-input and nacelle-yaw facts.
remarks: Both sets duplicate the filter-type claim (recursive single-pole low-pass with exponential smoothing) under two condition variants; this is a shared pattern rather than a differentiator. The filter equations (7-1), (7-2), (7-3a) and the definitions of alpha, n, Ts and fc are not claimed by either set.
